captions.instagram:
How do comets work?

A comet is a dark lump of dusty ice a few kilometres across that spends decades frozen in the dark. Ride Halley's comet along its real orbit, watch the ice wake up inside 3 AU, push dust grains with sunlight, blow the ion tail with the solar wind, and follow the dust down to the Perseids.

→ A comet’s heart is a dark lump of ice and dust a few kilometres across, as dark as charcoal.
→ Near the Sun its ice turns to gas, making a glowing coma and two tails, millions of kilometres long.
→ A comet rides a long ellipse: Halley’s goes from inside Venus’s orbit to beyond Neptune’s every 76 years.
→ Inside about 3 AU the sunlight turns its ice to gas, and the comet wakes up and grows its tails.
→ Sunlight pushes the dust and the solar wind blows the gas, so both tails point away from the Sun.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/cometclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do comets work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A comet is a dark lump of dusty ice a few kilometres across that spends decades frozen in the dark. Ride Halley's comet along its real orbit, watch the ice wake up inside 3 AU, push dust grains with sunlight, blow the ion tail with the solar wind, and follow the dust down to the Perseids.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/cometclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/cometclear

In this video:
• A dirty snowball with a dark crust. The nucleus is a few kilometres of ice, dust and dark organic material.
• A long ellipse and a wake-up. Halley's comet rides a needle-thin ellipse (a = 17.93 AU, e = 0.968, JPL) from 0.57 AU to 35 AU.
• Two tails, two pushes. Neither tail trails behind like smoke.
• Homes and endings. Comets are leftover planetesimals.
• Water, life and danger. Rosetta found more than three times Earth's heavy-hydrogen ratio in 67P's water, though comets Hartley 2 and 46P/Wirtanen match the oceans and a 2024 reanalysis questions 67P's value.
• Seeing and naming. Every 5 magnitudes is 100 times in brightness.
